label: IFNW1
finding: Reported secreted normal immune-cell protein, increased after activation.
decision_reason: Established normal immune protein production blocks unrestricted targeting and contributes to the shared-sequence exclusion background.
limitations: Relative protein signal is not TPM or absolute concentration. Culture composition and highly homologous interferons limit cell/paralog attribution; IFNA1/13 is explicitly shared. No therapeutic injury or peptide presentation demonstrated.

label: MRGPRX4
finding: Human normal DRG neurons show localized RNA and protein; approximately 6–8% of neurons are positive.
decision_reason: Direct normal neuronal protein evidence blocks unrestricted targeting.
limitations: Percentage of positive neurons is not TPM or a toxicity probability; functional inhibition differs from killing expressing cells.

label: CNGA2
finding: Normal human arterial endothelium and smooth muscle show localized CNGA2 RNA and protein.
decision_reason: Established non-permitted normal-cell protein blocks unrestricted direct targeting and shared-sequence clearance.
limitations: Evidence establishes normal production, not peptide presentation or clinical injury. No RNA concentration is inferred from protein detection. Patient-derived normal-appearing tissues and ex vivo activation do not describe all healthy resting donors.

label: SCN10A
finding: SCN10A is a marker of multiple normal human sensory-neuron populations with spatial validation.
decision_reason: A rare normal neural population is not represented adequately by the low routine-panel bulk maximum.
limitations: Human cell localization and established sensory-channel biology support screening exclusion; native atlas measurements are not converted to TPM and no clinical cytotoxicity is asserted.

label: GFRAL
finding: Normal human brainstem neurons express GFRAL.
decision_reason: Localized normal neuronal protein outweighs a low bulk-panel maximum.
limitations: Species-specific findings are distinguished from animal functional experiments. No TCR toxicity demonstrated.
